gloss: armor and helmet; suit of armor

definitions.gloss: armor and helmet; suit of armor
definitions.explanation: A complete set of Japanese warrior armor, including both the body armor ({甲|かぶと}) and helmet ({冑|かぶと}). Refers to the traditional armor worn by samurai and displayed as cultural artifacts in museums and during festivals.

examples.japanese: {博物館|はくぶつかん}に{甲冑|かっちゅう}が{展示|てんじ}されている。
examples.english: A suit of armor is on display at the museum.

examples.japanese: {武将|ぶしょう}が{甲冑|かっちゅう}を{身|み}にまとって{戦場|せんじょう}に{向|む}かった。
examples.english: The warrior donned his armor and headed to the battlefield.

examples.japanese: {端午|たんご}の{節句|せっく}には{甲冑|かっちゅう}を{飾|かざ}る{家|いえ}もある。
examples.english: Some families display a suit of armor for Boys' Day.

notes:
USAGE: {甲冑|かっちゅう} specifically refers to Japanese armor as a combined set of body protection ({甲|かぶと} or {鎧|よろい}) and helmet ({冑|かぶと}). It is commonly encountered in historical contexts, museum descriptions, and discussions of Japanese warrior culture.

During {端午|たんご}の{節句|せっく} (Boys' Day, May 5th), miniature {甲冑|かっちゅう} are displayed in homes to wish boys health and strength.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {甲冑|かっちゅう}を{身|み}にまとう: to don armor
- {甲冑|かっちゅう}を{飾|かざ}る: to display armor
- {甲冑|かっちゅう}{姿|すがた}: figure in armor

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {甲冑|かっちゅう}: full armor set (armor + helmet)
- {鎧|よろい}: body armor (without helmet)
- {兜|かぶと}: helmet
